questions.stem: Isiokwu 'Otu ụbọchị m na-agaghị echefu' dabara n'edemede
questions.explanation: A memorable day is recounted as a story: narrative essay (akụkọ).

questions.stem: Edemede na-akọwa otu ihe dị ka o si dị, dịka 'Ụlọ nna m', bụ edemede
questions.explanation: Describing a place or object as it is gives a descriptive essay (nkọwa).

questions.stem: N'akwụkwọ ozi i degaara onye isi ụlọakwụkwọ gị, ihe kwesịrị ịdị n'elu n'aka nri bụ
options: mbinye aka gị na aha gị zuru ezu
questions.explanation: The writer's address and the date go at the top right of a letter.

questions.stem: Edemede ebe mmadụ abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa na-ekwurịta okwu n'usoro bụ
questions.explanation: A written conversation between people is a dialogue (mkparịta ụka).

questions.stem: N'okwu 'egbe' na 'ọkụkọ', a hụrụ ndakọrịta ụdaume. Ụdaume ndị so 'o' n'otu bụ
questions.explanation: Igbo vowels fall into two harmony groups: a, ị, ọ, ụ and e, i, o, u.

questions.stem: Ọ bụrụ na e kewaa 'ụlọakwụkwọ' na mkpụrụokwu, ọnụọgụ ha ga-abụ
questions.explanation: ụ-lọ-a-kwụ-kwọ: five syllables (kw is a single consonant).

questions.stem: N'okwu 'mmiri', mkpụrụokwu nke mbụ bụ
questions.explanation: The first m is a syllabic nasal: m-mi-ri.

questions.stem: N'ide ụda, akara ( ¯ ) na-egosi
questions.explanation: The macron marks the downstep tone (ụda nsụda); acute marks high and grave marks low.

questions.stem: Kedu n'ime ndị a bụ otu mgbochiume e ji mkpụrụedemede abụọ dee?
questions.explanation: kp is a single consonant written with two letters, like ch, gb, gh, gw, kw, nw, ny and sh.

questions.stem: Ụdaume ole dị n'otu nke ọ bụla n'ime otu ndakọrịta ụdaume abụọ ahụ?
questions.explanation: Each harmony group has four vowels: a, ị, ọ, ụ and e, i, o, u.

questions.stem: Kedu nke n'ime ndị a abụghị ụdaume Igbo?
questions.explanation: y is a consonant; the eight vowels are a, e, i, ị, o, ọ, u, ụ.

questions.stem: N'ahịrịokwu 'Obi zụrụ akwụkwọ n'ahịa', ngwaa bụ
questions.explanation: zụrụ (bought) is the verb.

questions.stem: Nnọchiaha 'unu' na-anọchi anya
questions.explanation: unu is the second person plural pronoun.

questions.stem: 'Iri atọ na asaa' bụ
questions.explanation: Iri atọ (30) na asaa (7) = 37.

questions.stem: N'asụsụ Igbo, 'redio', 'tebụl' na 'kọmputa' bụ
questions.explanation: These words are borrowed from English (loan words).

questions.stem: Kedu ahịrịokwu na-egosi ihe ga-eme n'ọdịnihu?
questions.explanation: ga- marks the future.

questions.stem: N'ahịrịokwu 'Eze riri nri', akara '-ri' dị na 'riri' na-egosi
questions.explanation: The -rV suffix marks past time.

questions.stem: Kedu nke bụ njikọ n'ahịrịokwu 'Obi na Ada gara ahịa'?
questions.explanation: na (and) joins the two nouns.

questions.stem: Asụsụ Igbo e ji ede akwụkwọ, nke ndị Igbo niile na-aghọta, bụ
questions.explanation: Standard Igbo (Igbo Izugbe) is used in writing; local varieties are dialects (olumba).

questions.stem: 'Ilu bụ mmanụ e ji eri okwu' pụtara na ilu
options: na-eme ka okwu dị ụtọ ma doo anya
questions.explanation: Proverbs make speech pleasant and meaningful, as palm oil makes food enjoyable.

questions.stem: Anụmanụ a ma ama maka aghụghọ n'akụkọ ifo Igbo bụ
questions.explanation: Mbe (the tortoise) is the trickster of Igbo folktales.

questions.stem: 'Ihe nwere ụkwụ anọ ma ọ naghị aga ije' bụ ihe atụ nke
questions.explanation: It is a riddle (the answer could be a table or chair).

questions.stem: A na-esi n'ọnụ ebufe agụmagụ ọnụ site n'otu ọgbọ gaa n'ọgbọ ọzọ. Nke a pụtara na a naghị ebu ụzọ
questions.explanation: Oral literature is transmitted by word of mouth, not first written down.

questions.stem: Kedu nke bụ uru akụkọ ifo bara?
options: Ọ na-eme ka ụmụaka bụrụ ndị ohi
Ọ na-eme ka mmadụ kpọọ ibe ya asị
questions.explanation: Folktales teach moral lessons and entertain.

questions.stem: 'Egbe bere ugo bere' bụ
questions.explanation: It is a well-known proverb: let the kite perch and let the eagle perch.

questions.stem: Onye dere akwụkwọ akụkọ 'Ije Odumodu Jere'?
questions.explanation: Ije Odumodu Jere was written by Leopold Bell-Gam.

questions.stem: Onye dere akwụkwọ akụkọ 'Ukwa Ruo Oge Ya Ọ Daa'?
questions.explanation: Tony Ubesie wrote Ukwa Ruo Oge Ya Ọ Daa.

questions.stem: Onye na-ede abụ bụ
questions.explanation: A poet is ode abụ.

questions.stem: Ekele a na-ekele mmadụ n'ụtụtụ bụ
questions.explanation: Ị bọọla chi? is the morning greeting; Ka chi fọọ is said at night.

questions.stem: N'omenala Igbo, onye na-agọ ọjị n'ọgbakọ ụmụnwoke bụ
questions.explanation: Kola is blessed and broken by the eldest man present.

questions.stem: Ememe a na-enye nwa ọhụrụ aha bụ
questions.explanation: Iba nwa afa is the naming ceremony.

questions.stem: Chi egbe eluigwe n'okpukpe ọdịnala Igbo bụ
questions.explanation: Amadioha is associated with thunder; Ala is the earth deity.

questions.stem: Igba nkwu bụ ememe dị mkpa n'
questions.explanation: Igba nkwu (wine-carrying) is part of traditional marriage.

questions.stem: Egwuregwu ebe mmadụ abụọ na-agbalị ịkwatu ibe ha n'ala bụ
questions.explanation: Mgba is traditional wrestling.

questions.stem: Ọ bụrụ na mmadụ egbuo nwanne ya n'ụmụnna, a na-ewere ya dịka
questions.explanation: Killing a kinsman (ọchụ) is an abomination (arụ) against Ala.

questions.stem: Ememe ọdịnala a na-eme mgbe onye nwụrụ anwụ iji kwanyere ya ugwu ikpeazụ bụ
questions.explanation: Akwamozu is the funeral ceremony.

questions.stem: Otu ndị na-atụkọ ego, nke onye ọ bụla na-anara ya n'usoro, bụ
questions.explanation: Isusu is a rotating savings association.

questions.topic: Ewumewu mmekọrịta mmadụ na ibe ya
questions.stem: Otu ndị a mụrụ n'otu oge n'obodo, ndị na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, bụ
questions.explanation: An age grade (otu ọgbọ) groups people born within the same period.

questions.stem: Ngwa ofufe nke na-anọchi anya ike na mmeri nwoke n'ọrụ aka ya bụ
questions.explanation: Ikenga symbolises a man's strength and achievement through his right hand.

questions.stem: Ndị Awka ama ama n'akaọrụ
questions.explanation: Awka is famed for its blacksmiths (ụzụ).

questions.stem:
Họrọ otu n'ime isiokwu ndị a, dee edemede dị ihe dị ka okwu narị atọ:
(a) Uru ekwentị bara n'oge a.
(b) Ememe kacha atọ m ụtọ n'obodo m.
(c) Akwụkwọ ozi i degaara onye isi ụlọakwụkwọ gị maka ịrịọ ezumike ụbọchị atọ. [25 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Content: relevant, well-developed ideas suited to the essay type chosen
5 marks: Organisation: introduction, logical paragraphs, conclusion; formal letter layout with addresses, date, salutation and closing for (c)
7 marks: Expression: idiomatic Standard Igbo with apt proverbs and varied sentences
3 marks: Mechanical accuracy: standard orthography, spelling and punctuation
questions.explanation: (a) is argumentative/expository, (b) descriptive or narrative, (c) a formal letter. A good answer plans an introduction, focused paragraphs and a conclusion, uses idiomatic Standard Igbo with proverbs and follows the standard orthography.

questions.stem:
(a) Gịnị bụ mkpụrụokwu? [3 marks]
(b) Kọwaa ụdị nhazi mkpụrụokwu atọ dị n'Igbo, nye ihe atụ maka nke ọ bụla. [6 marks]
(c) Kọwaa ụda atọ dị n'Igbo na akara e ji egosi ha. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: A syllable is a unit of sound pronounced with one tone, built round a vowel or syllabic nasal
2 marks: Vowel alone (V), e.g. a in ala
2 marks: Consonant plus vowel (CV), e.g. la in ala
2 marks: Syllabic nasal (N), e.g. m in mmiri, n in nna
2 marks: High tone (ụda elu), marked with an acute accent
2 marks: Low tone (ụda ala), marked with a grave accent
2 marks: Downstep (ụda nsụda), marked with a macron
questions.explanation: A syllable carries one tone. Igbo syllables are V, CV and syllabic nasal N. Tones are high (´), low (`) and downstep (¯).

questions.stem:
(a) Gịnị bụ nnọchiaha? [2 marks]
(b) Dee nnọchiaha isii dị n'Igbo, gosi onye na ọnụọgụ nke ọ bụla. [6 marks]
(c) Gosi ọdịiche dị n'etiti Igbo Izugbe na olumba, nye uru Igbo Izugbe abụọ. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun
1 mark: m/mụ: first person singular
1 mark: ị/i: second person singular
1 mark: ọ/o: third person singular
1 mark: anyị: first person plural
1 mark: unu: second person plural
1 mark: ha: third person plural
3 marks: Igbo Izugbe is the standard variety used in writing, schools and media; olumba are local varieties spoken in particular areas
2 marks: Uru: unites speakers of different dialects
2 marks: Uru: used for writing books, teaching and examinations
questions.explanation: A pronoun replaces a noun: m, ị, ọ, anyị, unu, ha. Standard Igbo is the common written variety; dialects are local. Standard Igbo unites speakers and is used in education and writing.

questions.stem:
(a) Gịnị bụ ilu? [3 marks]
(b) Dee ilu atọ, kọwaa ihe nke ọ bụla pụtara. [9 marks]
(c) Dee uru ilu abụọ bara n'okwu Igbo. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: A proverb is a short, wise saying that expresses truth or experience in figurative language
3 marks: First proverb and meaning, e.g. Egbe bere ugo bere: live and let live
3 marks: Second proverb and meaning, e.g. Nwata kwọchaa aka, o soro okenye rie nri: a well-behaved youth is accepted among elders
3 marks: Third proverb and meaning, e.g. Onye wetara ọjị wetara ndụ: one who brings kola brings life/goodwill
2 marks: Proverbs make speech pleasant and show wisdom
1 mark: Proverbs teach morals and pass on experience
questions.explanation: A proverb is a short figurative saying of wisdom. Examples: Egbe bere ugo bere; Nwata kwọchaa aka o soro okenye rie nri; Onye wetara ọjị wetara ndụ. Proverbs beautify speech and teach morals.

questions.stem:
(a) Kọwaa otu e si anabata ọbịa n'ala Igbo. [9 marks]
(b) Gịnị mere ọjị ji dị mkpa n'omenala Igbo? [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: The host welcomes the guest with greetings such as Nnọọ and offers a seat
3 marks: Kola nut (ọjị) is presented, blessed and broken by the eldest man, often with ose (alligator pepper) or ugba
3 marks: Drinks or food are offered and the guest is seen off at departure
2 marks: Ọjị is a symbol of welcome, hospitality and goodwill
2 marks: It is used for prayers and blessings to Chukwu and the ancestors
2 marks: It shows peace, unity and respect in gatherings
questions.explanation: Guests are greeted with Nnọọ, seated, offered kola that the eldest blesses and breaks, then given food or drink. Kola symbolises welcome and goodwill and carries prayers for peace and unity.

questions.stem: Kọwaa ọrụ ụmụada na otu ọgbọ na-arụ n'ọchịchị obodo Igbo. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Ụmụada are daughters of the lineage married elsewhere
3 marks: Ụmụada settle disputes, especially among wives and families, and maintain peace
2 marks: Ụmụada perform roles at funerals and purify or correct wrongdoing in the family
3 marks: Otu ọgbọ are age grades of people born within the same period
2 marks: Age grades carry out community projects such as roads, markets and clearing paths
2 marks: Age grades enforce laws, provide security and punish offenders
questions.explanation: Ụmụada, daughters of the lineage, settle disputes and play key roles in funerals and family discipline. Age grades carry out public works, keep security and enforce community decisions.
